sourceSentences.text: ‘Take him to a healer, then,’ I heard Regal finally give the command.
‘See if he can work out what’s wrong with him.
Did one of you kick him in the head?’
I thought that he spoke of me, until I heard the sounds of Will being carried out.
So either I had got more into him than I had thought, or someone had kicked him in the head.
Perhaps his gasp had pulled it into his lungs.
I had no idea what it would do there.
As I felt his Skill presence fading, it was relief almost as blessed as surcease from pain.
Cautiously I relaxed my vigilance against him.
It was like setting down a terribly heavy weight.
Another thought blessed me.
They didn’t know.
No one had seen the paper and powder, it had happened too quickly for them.
They might not even think of poison until it was too late for him.
‘Is the Bastard dead?’
Regal demanded angrily.
‘If he is, I swear, every man of you will hang!’
Someone stooped hastily beside me, to lay fingers at the pulse in my throat.
‘He’s alive,’ a soldier said gruffly, almost sullenly.
Some day Regal would learn not to threaten his own guard.
I hoped he’d be taught it by an arrow through his back.
A moment later, someone dashed a bucket of cold water over me.
The shock of it jarred every pain I had to new frenzy.
I pulled my one eye open.
The first thing I saw was the water and blood on the floor in front of me.
If all that blood was mine, I was in trouble.
Dazedly, I tried to think of whose else it could be.
My mind did not seem to be working very well.
Time seemed to be flowing in jumps.
Regal was standing over me, angry and dishevelled, and then suddenly he was sitting in his chair.
In and out.
Light and dark and light again.
Someone knelt beside me, ran competent hands over me.
Burrich?
No. That was a dream from long ago.
This man had blue eyes and the nasal twang of a Farrow-man.
‘He’s bleeding a lot, King Regal.
But we can stop that.’
Someone put pressure on my brow.
A cup of watered wine held against my cracked lips, splashed into my mouth.
I choked on it.
‘You see, he’s alive.
I’d leave off, for today, your majesty.
I doubt if he’ll be able to answer any more questions before tomorrow.
He’ll just faint on you.’
A calm professional opinion.
Whoever it was stretched me out on the floor again and left.
A spasm rattled through me.
Seizure coming soon.
Good thing Will was gone.
Didn’t think I could keep my walls up through a seizure.
‘Oh, take him away,’ Regal said, disgusted and disappointed.
‘This has been nothing but a waste of my time today.’
His chair’s legs scraped on the floor as he left it.
I heard the sounds of his boots on the stone floor as he strode from the room.
Someone grabbed me by the shirt front, jerked me to my feet.
I could not even scream for the pain.
‘Stupid piece of dung,’ he snarled at me.
‘You’d better not die.
I’m not going to take lashes over the likes of you dying.’
‘Great threat, Verde,’ someone mocked him.
‘What are you going to do to him after he’s dead?’
‘Shut up.
It’ll be your back flayed to the bone as much as mine.
Let’s get him out of here and clean this up.’
The cell.
The blank wall of it.
They had left me on the floor, facing away from the door.
Somehow that seemed unfair of them.
I’d have to do all the work of rolling over just to see if they’d left me any water.
No. It was too much trouble.
Are you coming now?
I really want to, Nighteyes.
But I just don’t know how.
Changer.
Changer!
My brother!
Changer.
What is it?
You have been silent for so long.
Are you coming now?
I have been … silent?
Yes.
I thought you had died, without coming to me first.
I could not reach you.
Probably a seizure.
I didn’t know it had happened.
But now I am right here, Nighteyes.
Right here.
Then come to me.
Hurry, before you die.
A moment.
Let us be sure of this.
I tried to think of a reason not to.
I knew there had been some, but I could no longer recall them.
Changer, he had called me.
My own wolf, calling me that, just as the Fool or Chade called me a catalyst.
Well.
Time to change things for Regal.
The last thing I could do was make sure I died before Regal broke me.
If I had to go down, I would do it alone.
No words of mine would implicate anyone else.
I hoped the dukes would demand to see my body.
It took a long time to get my arm from the floor to my chest.
My lips were cracked and swollen, my teeth aching in my gums.
But I put my shirt cuff to my mouth, and found the tiny lump of the leaf pellet inside the fabric.
I bit down at it as hard as I could, then sucked on it.
After a moment, the taste of carryme flooded my mouth.
It was not unpleasant.
Pungent.
As the herb deadened the pain in my mouth, I could chew at my sleeve more strongly.
Stupidly, I tried to be careful of the porcupine quill.
Didn’t want to get a quill in my lip.
It really hurts when that happens.
I know, Nighteyes.
Come to me.
I’m trying.
Give me a moment.
How does one leave one’s body behind?
I tried to ignore it, to be aware of myself only as Nighteyes.
Keen nose.
Lying on my side, chewing diligently at a lump of snow wadded up in the space between my toes.
I tasted snow and my own paw as I nibbled and licked it away.
I looked up.
Evening coming on.
It would soon be a good time to hunt.
I stood up, shook myself all over.
That’s right, Nighteyes encouraged me.
But there was still that thread, that tiny awareness of a stiff and aching body on a cold stone floor.
Just to think of it made it more real.
A tremor ran through it, rattling its bones and teeth.
Seizure coming.
Big one this time.
Suddenly, it was all so easy.
Such an easy choice.
Leave that body for this one.
It didn’t work very well any more anyway.
Stuck in a cage.
No point to keeping it.
No point to being a man at all.
I’m here.
I know.
Let us hunt.
And we did.

sourceParagraphs.text: ‘Take him to a healer, then,’ I heard Regal finally give the command. ‘See if he can work out what’s wrong with him. Did one of you kick him in the head?’

I thought that he spoke of me, until I heard the sounds of Will being carried out. So either I had got more into him than I had thought, or someone had kicked him in the head. Perhaps his gasp had pulled it into his lungs. I had no idea what it would do there. As I felt his Skill presence fading, it was relief almost as blessed as surcease from pain. Cautiously I relaxed my vigilance against him. It was like setting down a terribly heavy weight. Another thought blessed me. They didn’t know. No one had seen the paper and powder, it had happened too quickly for them. They might not even think of poison until it was too late for him.
‘Is the Bastard dead?’ Regal demanded angrily. ‘If he is, I swear, every man of you will hang!’

Someone stooped hastily beside me, to lay fingers at the pulse in my throat. ‘He’s alive,’ a soldier said gruffly, almost sullenly. Some day Regal would learn not to threaten his own guard. I hoped he’d be taught it by an arrow through his back.

A moment later, someone dashed a bucket of cold water over me. The shock of it jarred every pain I had to new frenzy. I pulled my one eye open. The first thing I saw was the water and blood on the floor in front of me. If all that blood was mine, I was in trouble. Dazedly, I tried to think of whose else it could be. My mind did not seem to be working very well. Time seemed to be flowing in jumps. Regal was standing over me, angry and dishevelled, and then suddenly he was sitting in his chair. In and out. Light and dark and light again.

Someone knelt beside me, ran competent hands over me. Burrich? No. That was a dream from long ago. This man had blue eyes and the nasal twang of a Farrow-man. ‘He’s bleeding a lot, King Regal. But we can stop that.’ Someone put pressure on my brow. A cup of watered wine held against my cracked lips, splashed into my mouth. I choked on it. ‘You see, he’s alive. I’d leave off, for today, your majesty. I doubt if he’ll be able to answer any more questions before tomorrow. He’ll just faint on you.’ A calm professional opinion. Whoever it was stretched me out on the floor again and left.
A spasm rattled through me. Seizure coming soon. Good thing Will was gone. Didn’t think I could keep my walls up through a seizure.

‘Oh, take him away,’ Regal said, disgusted and disappointed. ‘This has been nothing but a waste of my time today.’ His chair’s legs scraped on the floor as he left it. I heard the sounds of his boots on the stone floor as he strode from the room.

Someone grabbed me by the shirt front, jerked me to my feet. I could not even scream for the pain. ‘Stupid piece of dung,’ he snarled at me. ‘You’d better not die. I’m not going to take lashes over the likes of you dying.’
‘Great threat, Verde,’ someone mocked him. ‘What are you going to do to him after he’s dead?’
‘Shut up. It’ll be your back flayed to the bone as much as mine. Let’s get him out of here and clean this up.’

The cell. The blank wall of it. They had left me on the floor, facing away from the door. Somehow that seemed unfair of them. I’d have to do all the work of rolling over just to see if they’d left me any water.
No. It was too much trouble.
Are you coming now?
I really want to, Nighteyes. But I just don’t know how.
Changer. Changer! My brother! Changer.
What is it?
You have been silent for so long. Are you coming now?
I have been … silent?
Yes. I thought you had died, without coming to me first. I could not reach you.
Probably a seizure. I didn’t know it had happened. But now I am right here, Nighteyes. Right here.
Then come to me. Hurry, before you die.
A moment. Let us be sure of this.

I tried to think of a reason not to. I knew there had been some, but I could no longer recall them. Changer, he had called me. My own wolf, calling me that, just as the Fool or Chade called me a catalyst. Well. Time to change things for Regal. The last thing I could do was make sure I died before Regal broke me. If I had to go down, I would do it alone. No words of mine would implicate anyone else. I hoped the dukes would demand to see my body.

It took a long time to get my arm from the floor to my chest. My lips were cracked and swollen, my teeth aching in my gums. But I put my shirt cuff to my mouth, and found the tiny lump of the leaf pellet inside the fabric. I bit down at it as hard as I could, then sucked on it. After a moment, the taste of carryme flooded my mouth. It was not unpleasant. Pungent. As the herb deadened the pain in my mouth, I could chew at my sleeve more strongly. Stupidly, I tried to be careful of the porcupine quill. Didn’t want to get a quill in my lip.
It really hurts when that happens.
I know, Nighteyes.
Come to me.
I’m trying. Give me a moment.

How does one leave one’s body behind? I tried to ignore it, to be aware of myself only as Nighteyes. Keen nose. Lying on my side, chewing diligently at a lump of snow wadded up in the space between my toes. I tasted snow and my own paw as I nibbled and licked it away. I looked up. Evening coming on. It would soon be a good time to hunt. I stood up, shook myself all over.
That’s right, Nighteyes encouraged me.

But there was still that thread, that tiny awareness of a stiff and aching body on a cold stone floor. Just to think of it made it more real. A tremor ran through it, rattling its bones and teeth. Seizure coming. Big one this time.
Suddenly, it was all so easy. Such an easy choice. Leave that body for this one. It didn’t work very well any more anyway. Stuck in a cage. No point to keeping it. No point to being a man at all.
I’m here.
I know. Let us hunt.
And we did.

Кто-то схватил меня за грудки и рывком поднял на ноги. Я даже не мог закричать от боли. — Тупой кусок дерьма, — прорычал он мне. — Только не вздумай умирать. Я не собираюсь получать плетей из-за того, что такой, как ты, подохнет.
— Грозно сказано, Верде, — насмешливо заметил кто-то. — И что ты с ним сделаешь, когда он уже умрёт?
— Заткнись. Твою спину сдерут до костей не меньше, чем мою. Давайте вытащим его отсюда и приберём здесь.

Камера. Её голая стена. Меня оставили на полу лицом от двери. Почему-то это показалось мне с их стороны несправедливым. Мне пришлось бы проделать всю работу: перекатиться, лишь чтобы увидеть, оставили ли мне воды.
Нет. Слишком много хлопот.
Ты идёшь теперь?
Я правда хочу, Ночной Волк. Но я просто не знаю как.
Изменяющий. Изменяющий! Мой брат! Изменяющий.
Что такое?
Ты так долго молчал. Ты идёшь теперь?
Я был… молчал?
Да. Я думал, ты умер, не придя сперва ко мне. Я не мог до тебя достучаться.
Наверное, припадок. Я не знал, что он случился. Но теперь я здесь, Ночной Волк. Прямо здесь.
Тогда иди ко мне. Спеши, пока не умер.
Минуточку. Давай удостоверимся.

Я попытался придумать причину этого не делать. Я знал, что причины были, но больше не мог их вспомнить. Он назвал меня Изменяющим. Мой собственный волк называл меня так же, как Шут или Чейд называли меня катализатором. Что ж. Пора было изменить кое-что для Регала. Последнее, что я мог сделать, — позаботиться, чтобы я умер прежде, чем Регал меня сломает. Если мне суждено пасть, я сделаю это один. Ни одно моё слово не впутает никого другого. Я надеялся, герцоги потребуют показать моё тело.

Прошло много времени, прежде чем мне удалось поднять руку с пола к груди. Губы у меня потрескались и распухли, зубы ныли в дёснах. Но я поднёс манжету рубашки ко рту и нащупал крошечный комочек листовой пилюли внутри ткани. Я как можно сильнее впился в него зубами, а затем стал сосать. Через мгновение вкус керрими наполнил рот. Он не был неприятен. Едкий. Когда трава притупила боль во рту, я смог сильнее жевать рукав. По-глупому я старался не задеть иглу дикобраза. Не хотел загнать иглу в губу.
Это правда очень больно, когда такое случается.
Я знаю, Ночной Волк.
Иди ко мне.
Я пытаюсь. Дай мне минуту.

Как оставить позади собственное тело? Я попытался не замечать его, сознавать себя только как Ночного Волка. Острый нос. Лежу на боку, усердно разгрызаю комок снега, набившийся между пальцами лап. Я ощущал вкус снега и собственной лапы, обгрызая и слизывая его. Я поднял голову. Вечер близится. Скоро будет самое время охотиться. Я встал, отряхнулся всем телом.
Вот так, подбодрил меня Ночной Волк.

Но всё ещё тянулась та нить, то крошечное осознание окоченевшего, ноющего тела на холодном каменном полу. Стоило подумать о нём — и оно становилось реальнее. По нему пробежала дрожь, застучали кости и зубы. Припадок начинается. На этот раз сильный.
Внезапно всё стало так просто. Такой лёгкий выбор. Оставить то тело ради этого. Всё равно оно уже почти не годилось. Заперто в клетке. Незачем его сохранять. Незачем вообще быть человеком.
Я здесь.
Я знаю. Давай охотиться.
И мы охотились.

paragraphPairs.sourceText: I thought that he spoke of me, until I heard the sounds of Will being carried out. So either I had got more into him than I had thought, or someone had kicked him in the head. Perhaps his gasp had pulled it into his lungs. I had no idea what it would do there. As I felt his Skill presence fading, it was relief almost as blessed as surcease from pain. Cautiously I relaxed my vigilance against him. It was like setting down a terribly heavy weight. Another thought blessed me. They didn’t know. No one had seen the paper and powder, it had happened too quickly for them. They might not even think of poison until it was too late for him.
paragraphPairs.translatedText: Я подумал, что он говорит обо мне, пока не услышал, как Уилла выносят. Значит, либо я всыпал ему больше, чем думал, либо кто-то пнул его по голове. Возможно, при вдохе порошок попал ему в лёгкие. Я понятия не имел, что он там сделает. Когда его присутствие в Скилле стало угасать, я ощутил облегчение почти столь же благословенное, как прекращение боли. Я осторожно ослабил бдительность против него. Это было словно сбросить ужасно тяжёлую ношу. Затем меня осенила другая благословенная мысль. Они не знали. Никто не видел бумаги и порошка: всё произошло слишком быстро. Они могли даже не подумать о яде, пока не станет слишком поздно для него.

paragraphPairs.sourceText: A moment later, someone dashed a bucket of cold water over me. The shock of it jarred every pain I had to new frenzy. I pulled my one eye open. The first thing I saw was the water and blood on the floor in front of me. If all that blood was mine, I was in trouble. Dazedly, I tried to think of whose else it could be. My mind did not seem to be working very well. Time seemed to be flowing in jumps. Regal was standing over me, angry and dishevelled, and then suddenly he was sitting in his chair. In and out. Light and dark and light again.
paragraphPairs.translatedText: Мгновение спустя кто-то вылил на меня ведро холодной воды. От потрясения каждая моя боль взбесилась с новой силой. Я приоткрыл единственный глаз. Первым делом я увидел воду и кровь на полу перед собой. Если вся эта кровь была моей, дела мои плохи. Ошеломлённо я попытался подумать, чьей ещё она могла быть. Мысли, похоже, работали не слишком хорошо. Время словно текло скачками. Регал стоял надо мной, злой и растрёпанный, а потом вдруг уже сидел в кресле. То здесь, то нет. Свет, тьма и снова свет.

paragraphPairs.sourceText: It took a long time to get my arm from the floor to my chest. My lips were cracked and swollen, my teeth aching in my gums. But I put my shirt cuff to my mouth, and found the tiny lump of the leaf pellet inside the fabric. I bit down at it as hard as I could, then sucked on it. After a moment, the taste of carryme flooded my mouth. It was not unpleasant. Pungent. As the herb deadened the pain in my mouth, I could chew at my sleeve more strongly. Stupidly, I tried to be careful of the porcupine quill. Didn’t want to get a quill in my lip.
paragraphPairs.translatedText: Прошло много времени, прежде чем мне удалось поднять руку с пола к груди. Губы у меня потрескались и распухли, зубы ныли в дёснах. Но я поднёс манжету рубашки ко рту и нащупал крошечный комочек листовой пилюли внутри ткани. Я как можно сильнее впился в него зубами, а затем стал сосать. Через мгновение вкус керрими наполнил рот. Он не был неприятен. Едкий. Когда трава притупила боль во рту, я смог сильнее жевать рукав. По-глупому я старался не задеть иглу дикобраза. Не хотел загнать иглу в губу.

paragraphPairs.sourceText: How does one leave one’s body behind? I tried to ignore it, to be aware of myself only as Nighteyes. Keen nose. Lying on my side, chewing diligently at a lump of snow wadded up in the space between my toes. I tasted snow and my own paw as I nibbled and licked it away. I looked up. Evening coming on. It would soon be a good time to hunt. I stood up, shook myself all over.
paragraphPairs.translatedText: Как оставить позади собственное тело? Я попытался не замечать его, сознавать себя только как Ночного Волка. Острый нос. Лежу на боку, усердно разгрызаю комок снега, набившийся между пальцами лап. Я ощущал вкус снега и собственной лапы, обгрызая и слизывая его. Я поднял голову. Вечер близится. Скоро будет самое время охотиться. Я встал, отряхнулся всем телом.
